subject: Potential third-party patent notice re: generated outputs — indemnity & SLA fallback
messages:
From: Alice Ngo <alice.ngo@futurahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@futurahealth.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Third-party patent notice re: outputs from your model

Hi Jonas / Karthik,

We received a notice this morning from counsel for VertexBio alleging that a sequence of outputs generated by your API (attached sample) infringes a patent they hold. This was raised by an internal research group after a user provided the output as part of a clinical writeup.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the outputs in the attached sample were generated by models in our provisioned environment? We have attached the sample output and the claim notice (claim_notice_0917.pdf).
- We need a point of contact for evidence preservation (logs, model id, prompt).
- Due to legal risk, Procurement is asking to temporarily pause the specific feature in our integration unless we have a mitigation plan.

Futura is requesting indemnity under the MSA for third-party claims caused by your service. Please advise next steps and a timeline for evidence handoff.

Thanks,
Alice Ngo
Legal & Compliance — Futura Health
Alice.Ngo@futurahealth.com

Attachment: claim_notice_0917.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ngo <alice.ngo@futurahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Third-party patent notice re: outputs from your model

Alice — thanks for flagging and for the materials. We take third-party claims seriously. Looping in our legal lead Kimberly and engineering lead Karthik so we can coordinate evidence and mitigation.

Proposed immediate steps:
1) Preservation: We will preserve logs, model id, and request/response payloads for the time window in your sample. Please confirm the timestamps in the sample (or attach any additional examples).
2) Temporary mitigation: We can disable the model endpoint for your tenant (or add a model-level opt-out) within 2 hours if you want an operational pause. We can also route production traffic to an older model variant as a canary fallback to reduce exposure while we investigate.
3) Evidence handoff: Kimberly — can you own the indemnity/Q&A with Futura counsel? I understand procurement wants to pause until we have a plan; we should document a mutual action plan to keep the integration stable for other customers.

Alice — can you confirm whether you want Redwood to disable the endpoint while we investigate?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

> On Thu, Sep 17, 2026 at 9:12 AM Alice Ngo <alice.ngo@futurahealth.com> wrote:
> > [claim_notice_0917.pdf attached]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ngo <alice.ngo@futurahealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@futurahealth.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Third-party patent notice re: outputs from your model — next steps and MSA redline

Alice / team — I reviewed the claim notice and initial sample. I want to outline the legal posture and suggested short-term commercial concessions so we can be transparent:

Legal posture (short):
- Redwood's current MSA (v2.1) has a standard third-party infringement indemnity but with carveouts for AI-generated outputs that are user prompts-derived content. We need to confirm whether the alleged infringing material arose from customer-provided content or purely model hallucination.
- For a production claim we will expect cooperation (notice, opportunity to defend) and will evaluate whether defense-control should be exercised by Redwood or Futura depending on coverage and alignment with insurers.

Suggested immediate actions for the MAP (mutual action plan):
- Evidence exchange: Redwood will provide preserved request/response logs, model id, timestamped call traces, and a package of the sample outputs by EOD tomorrow. We will provide a secure Drive folder (link below).
- Scope narrowing: propose to negotiate a narrow indemnity carveout limiting Redwood's obligation to direct infringement by model weights/core outputs (not downstream derivative uses), and to exclude claims arising from customer-supplied prompts or post-processed outputs.
- Defense control compromise: propose hybrid approach — Redwood offers to defend where the claim alleges direct infringement of model outputs but reserves step-in rights if defense materially alters technical approach.
- Short-term commercial: propose a limited SLA exception/credit for impacted calls while mitigation is active (proposal: one-time credit applied if Redwood disables endpoint at customer's request; amount to be routed through Sales ops).

I attached a marked-up MSA indemnity redline for your procurement and counsel to review: MSA_indemnity_redline_jonas_20260917.docx.

Operational note to Engineering (Karthik): we will need a technical snapshot (model hash, weights identifier, sequence length, KV cache logs, whether the model was fine-tuned on customer data). Please preserve and share via secure folder.

Alice — can you confirm whether Futura counsel prefers Redwood to assume defense control initially or to require mutual approval for lead counsel? That choice affects timing.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folder/0B_sample_evidence

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: MSA_indemnity_redline_jonas_20260917.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Alice Ngo <alice.ngo@futurahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@futurahealth.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Third-party patent notice re: outputs from your model — engineering notes

Quick technical update / options from infra side:
- Preservation: we have snapshot exports for Futura's tenant for 2026-09-15T12:00:00Z through 2026-09-17T08:00:00Z. We can hand over sanitized logs (timestamps, model id, non-sensitive prompt snippets) within 6 business hours. Full request/response stacks will require a CII request and DPA confirmation; Kimberly can advise.
- Mitigation options we can enact today:
  * Disable the specific model endpoint for Futura (near-zero risk) — rollback available within 30 minutes.
  * Canary fallback: route Futura traffic to a legacy, smaller model variant that has different tokenization and lower similarity likelihood; we can enable this as a traffic-split (10% -> 100%) within 1 hour.
  * Prompt sanitization layer: we can insert a pre-call filter to strip certain user-provided sequences (requires consent).
- Logging: we will preserve KV cache snapshots and session-level traces as requested. Please state whether you want us to preserve raw prompts or redacted prompts.

Operational ask: if Procurement requests an endpoint pause, please authorize in writing so we can act immediately. Also note that disabling the endpoint will disrupt live features; suggest a canary fallback unless Futura mandates a full pause.

Thanks,
Karthik
Eng Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

To: Alice Ngo <alice.ngo@futurahealth.com>, procurement@futurahealth.com

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MAP and commercial path forward — Futura / Redwood (DW-2391)

Hi Alice / procurement team — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Below is a concise mutual action plan we can use to converge this week. If this looks good we will route the commercial items through Sales Ops for approval.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — high level:
- Today (Fri EOD): Redwood to preserve logs and upload sanitized evidence package to secure Drive. (Owner: Redwood infra; ETA: 6 hours)
- Today: Redwood can enable a canary fallback for 10% traffic immediately; full toggle to disable endpoint available on written instruction from Futura (Owner: Karthik / Ops)
- Tomorrow: Legal to exchange positions on defense-control and indemnity carveouts based on Redwood's redline doc. Kimberly to provide one-page summary for Futura counsel by 10:00 AM PT. (Owner: Kimberly)
- Commercial: Sales to prepare proposed one-time credit (to be used if Redwood disables endpoint at customer's request) and optional short-term SLA exception while remediation is ongoing. (Owner: Jonas / Sales Ops)

Suggested short-term commercial parameters (for negotiation):
- One-time service credit equal to two weeks of average monthly spend for impacted calls, applied upon endpoint disablement at customer request.
- Escrow / evidence deposit workflow: if claim proceeds, funds/escrow mechanics to be discussed — Redwood is open to limited escrow threshold tied to materiality.

Please reply with: (A) whether Futura wants the endpoint disabled immediately, (B) whether we should route full logs (requires DPA/CII confirmation), and (C) whether procurement needs a formal credit memo to allow continued service.

Thanks — we will standby for written authorizations and will not make unilateral defense decisions without mutual counsel alignment.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
